request: Detailed instructions for making, storing, timing and applying preparations 500–508 in the online course

authoring.method: Original bilingual teaching based on the supplied book methods and separately attributed later practitioner protocols; no source prose reproduced at length
sourceSeparation: Classical manufacturing methods follow Courtney’s introduction and GA 327 lectures 4–6/discussions
Metric spray examples and weighed compost-set example attributed to Bucher’s 2020 manual
501 metric example cross-checked against Brazilian ABD guidance
JPI supplied-set placement and two horsetail recipes kept distinct
No asserted universal equivalence between supplier volume units and preparation mass
authoring.coreScope: Classical preparations 500–508; proprietary compound products, disease diagnosis and legal certification have their own requirements

500Example.source: Bucher manual, pp. 23–24; selected 50 L end of 25–50 L range

501Example.source: Bucher pp. 23–24 and ABD 501 technical directions

compostWeighedExample.source: Bucher pp. 65–66; not converted to a universal volumetric rate

numericalReview.compostSuppliedSet: JPI whole supplied set; six distributed holes, half-depth; 507 in one US gallon stirred 10 minutes; half internal and half over surface; original ton unit qualified
numericalReview.508Fresh: JPI 1.5 oz dried herb in one US quart, simmer one hour, cool/strain, add two US gallons, stir 20 minutes, foliar; metric amounts explicitly approximate
numericalReview.508Fermented: JPI same herb amount in one US gallon, simmer one hour, cool; loose-lid fermentation 10–14 days; one part concentrate plus nine water, stir 20 minutes, soil
unitChecks: 500 and 501 duration retained at one hour irrespective of area
US customary 508 conversions are approximate; evaporation not ignored

handlingContext: Traceable permitted animal materials and trained handling of skull/casings
No unsupervised dry quartz grinding; respiratory silica hazard identified
Manure appearance/odour not treated as pathogen tests
Food-crop and manure-derived-input requirements left to applicable local rules, not a fabricated universal harvest interval
Fermentation pressure and venting distinguished from stable bottle storage
Horsetail identification and fresh versus fermented targets kept distinct
integration: Visible practical-companion entry on What Is Biodynamics? and Agriculture overviews
Progressive enhancement; all teaching and static calculations readable without JavaScript
Calculator performs only arithmetic for one named metric example; no stored personal data
Original compost diagram is labelled as a course schematic, not Steiner’s drawing

preservation.result: All hashes match the pre-task snapshot; existing quoted texts, detailed source records and seven original book illustrations unchanged

limits: No field trial or learner study
Guides describe practice; do not establish spiritual mechanisms, pathogen reduction or disease-control efficacy
